# Coverly ROMs

> Free desktop app (AGPL-3.0-only) for Windows, macOS and Linux that audits a ROM library, such as a handheld's SD card, shows which games lack cover, screenshot or title-screen art, and fills them in bulk from libretro-thumbnails (no account) or SteamGridDB (your own key). A dry run comes first, existing art is never overwritten unless you ask (and then it is backed up), and the last job can be undone. It ships with a command line, `coverly`. No account, no telemetry. Made by Miguel Esparza (MAECLY).

Canonical: https://coverly-roms.maecly.com/
English page: https://coverly-roms.maecly.com/en/
Source: https://github.com/MAECLY/coverly-roms

No version is published yet; the first one is being prepared. Until then it can be built from source (see the README). Releases: https://github.com/MAECLY/coverly-roms/releases
<!-- norelease:end -->

Builds carry no Apple or Microsoft code-signing certificate, so macOS Gatekeeper ("Open Anyway") and Windows SmartScreen ("More info", then "Run anyway") warn the first time. Downloads can be checked against SHA256SUMS.

## What it does today

- Audit: scans a library (systems, ROMs including multi-file .cue/.bin, .m3u, .gdi and folder games) and reports, per media type (cover, screenshot, title screen), what is present or missing. Read-only. Exports CSV or JSON.
- Layout profiles, detected automatically: Anbernic stock, GarlicOS, Onion OS, MinUI / NextUI (cover); muOS (cover, screenshot); ES-DE, RetroArch (cover, screenshot, title); Batocera / Knulli / EmulationStation (cover, screenshot, title, plus gamelist.xml merging with undo). Custom profiles with your own path templates and a live preview.
- More than 50 known systems with the folder aliases each firmware uses.
- Identification: CRC32, MD5 and SHA1 against libretro-database, then the file name; arcade short names through MAME and FBNeo DATs. Method selectable: hash-then-name, hash-only, name-only. .7z archives are identified by name only.
- Sources: libretro-thumbnails (default, no account); SteamGridDB (optional, your own API key, kept in the OS keychain).
- Choosing the image: by the ROM's region (default order rom, world, usa, europe, japan), by source priority, or by popularity (SteamGridDB votes, then agreement between sources). Each choice says why.
- Safety: dry run by default; only missing art by default; existing art replaced only if you choose overwrite-with-backup; nothing written outside the library folder; atomic writes; backups and job journals in the app data folder, not on the card; undo of the last job; uncertain matches go to a keyboard-driven review queue; jobs pause, resume and cancel; one failing item never stops a job; offline or rate-limited jobs pause; file names safe for FAT/exFAT; macOS ._ files ignored.
- App: library browser (folders, systems, date, all), virtualised grid and table with filters and search, a detail panel per game (change, search, from file, remove), fill wizard, connected drives on the start screen, English and Spanish, light/dark/system themes.
- CLI: coverly audit, fill (dry run unless --apply; --auto-only skips review items), profiles, systems, undo, update.
- Privacy: no telemetry. Network requests only to the art sources and the optional update check. Images are decoded and re-encoded, which strips metadata.
- Updates: in-app, from GitHub Releases, verified with minisign; stable and beta channels; never restarts during a job.

## Not supported

- ScreenScraper (planned; not available in public builds).
- TheGamesDB; mixed/composite images, videos, marquees, wheels.
- Editing gamelist metadata, renaming or verifying ROMs.
- Running on the handheld itself.
- It bundles no ROMs, BIOS files or game art. Game art belongs to its owners.
- Not yet tested on real handhelds; the maximum image sizes some firmware accepts are not confirmed.
